lines.raw: Lesson 1: What is a Pharmacy Claim?
lines.say: Lesson 1: What is a Pharmacy Claim?

lines.raw: Every prescription filled at a pharmacy leaves a record: a pharmacy claim.
lines.say: Every prescription filled at a pharmacy leaves a record: a pharmacy claim.

lines.raw: All those claims together are pharmacy data.
lines.say: All those claims together are pharmacy data.

lines.raw: In this lesson you will:
lines.say: In this lesson you will:

lines.raw: Explain in one sentence what a pharmacy claim is, and what "pharmacy data" means.
lines.say: Explain in one sentence what a pharmacy claim is, and what "pharmacy data" means.

lines.raw: See how buying medicine in Nepal compares to filling a prescription in the US.
lines.say: See how buying medicine in Nepal compares to filling a prescription in the U S.

lines.raw: Tell the pharmacy benefit from the medical benefit.
lines.say: Tell the pharmacy benefit from the medical benefit.

lines.raw: Start with something you already know.
lines.say: Start with something you already know.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: After a doctor visit in Nepal, you walk out with a **prescription paper** (the "parchi").
lines.say: After a doctor visit in Nepal, you walk out with a prescription paper (the "parchi").

lines.raw: You take it to a **medical shop** outside the hospital, or to the **hospital pharmacy**, and buy the medicines.
lines.say: You take it to a medical shop outside the hospital, or to the hospital pharmacy, and buy the medicines.

lines.raw: The shopkeeper gives you the medicine and a **bill**.
lines.say: The shopkeeper gives you the medicine and a bill.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: That bill records **which medicine**, **how much**, **how strong**, **who prescribed it**, **when** you bought it and **how much it cost**.
lines.say: That bill records which medicine, how much, how strong, who prescribed it, when you bought it and how much it cost.

lines.raw: In the US, the same details are sent to an insurance company as a **prescription drug claim**.
lines.say: In the U S, the same details are sent to an insurance company as a prescription drug claim.

lines.raw: All of these claims together are **pharmacy data**.
lines.say: All of these claims together are pharmacy data.

scenes.section: Start with something you already know

lines.raw: Simple definition.
lines.say: Simple definition.

lines.raw: Pharmacy data is the record of prescription medicines a patient picked up from a pharmacy, written in a way that an insurance company can read and pay for.
lines.say: Pharmacy data is the record of prescription medicines a patient picked up from a pharmacy, written in a way that an insurance company can read and pay for.

lines.raw: Our three people buy medicine.
lines.say: Our three people buy medicine.

lines.raw: This course follows three people.
lines.say: This course follows three people.

lines.raw: **Ram** works at a tech startup in Kathmandu and has private health insurance.
lines.say: Ram works at a tech startup in Kathmandu and has private health insurance.

lines.raw: **Sita** is an accountant in Kathmandu who contributes to the Social Security Fund (SSF).
lines.say: Sita is an accountant in Kathmandu who contributes to the Social Security Fund (S S F).

lines.raw: **Emily** is an office worker in Texas, USA, with health insurance through her employer.
lines.say: Emily is an office worker in Texas, U S A, with health insurance through her employer.

lines.raw: All three had a sore throat with fever, and the doctor found **strep throat**.
lines.say: All three had a sore throat with fever, and the doctor found strep throat.

lines.raw: Each of them now needs an **antibiotic**.
lines.say: Each of them now needs an antibiotic.

lines.raw: In Nepal: Ram and Sita buy their antibiotics.
lines.say: In Nepal: Ram and Sita buy their antibiotics.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: **Ram** takes his prescription to a medical shop near the hospital and buys the antibiotic.
lines.say: Ram takes his prescription to a medical shop near the hospital and buys the antibiotic.

lines.raw: He **pays the full price** at the counter and asks for a proper **pharmacy bill** with the medicine name, quantity and price.
lines.say: He pays the full price at the counter and asks for a proper pharmacy bill with the medicine name, quantity and price.

lines.raw: Later he sends that bill, **with the prescription**, to his insurer.
lines.say: Later he sends that bill, with the prescription, to his insurer.

lines.raw: The insurer checks that the medicine matches the prescription and **reimburses** him.
lines.say: The insurer checks that the medicine matches the prescription and reimburses him.

lines.raw: Without the prescription, the insurer would not know a doctor ordered it.
lines.say: Without the prescription, the insurer would not know a doctor ordered it.

lines.raw: That is why Ram keeps both papers.
lines.say: That is why Ram keeps both papers.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: **Sita** gets her medicine from the **pharmacy of the SSF-listed hospital** where she was treated.
lines.say: Sita gets her medicine from the pharmacy of the S S F listed hospital where she was treated.

lines.raw: She shows her SSF ID and pays her **20%** share for the medicines covered by SSF.
lines.say: She shows her S S F I D and pays her 20 percent share for the medicines covered by S S F.

lines.raw: The hospital adds the medicine to the bill it sends to SSF, and **SSF pays the other 80%**.
lines.say: The hospital adds the medicine to the bill it sends to S S F, and S S F pays the other 80 percent.

lines.raw: In the US: Emily picks up her antibiotic in Texas.
lines.say: In the U S: Emily picks up her antibiotic in Texas.

lines.raw: On **10 March 2025**, Dr. Patel sends Emily's prescription for **amoxicillin** straight to the pharmacy's computer (an **e-prescription**).
lines.say: On 10 March 2025, Doctor Patel sends Emily's prescription for amoxicillin straight to the pharmacy's computer (an e-prescription).

lines.raw: At the counter, Emily shows her **insurance card**.
lines.say: At the counter, Emily shows her insurance card.

lines.raw: The pharmacist types in the card details.
lines.say: The pharmacist types in the card details.

lines.raw: The pharmacy's computer **sends a claim electronically** to her plan.
lines.say: The pharmacy's computer sends a claim electronically to her plan.

lines.raw: Within a few **seconds**, the answer comes back: covered, and Emily pays **$5**.
lines.say: Within a few seconds, the answer comes back: covered, and Emily pays 5 dollars.

lines.raw: Emily pays her $5 and walks out with the medicine.
lines.say: Emily pays her 5 dollars and walks out with the medicine.

lines.raw: The plan pays the rest to the pharmacy later.
lines.say: The plan pays the rest to the pharmacy later.

lines.raw: The big idea: the claim happens at the counter.
lines.say: The big idea: the claim happens at the counter.

lines.raw: A US **medical** claim is usually sent **days after** the visit, and the patient waits to learn what they owe.
lines.say: A U S medical claim is usually sent days after the visit, and the patient waits to learn what they owe.

lines.raw: A US **pharmacy** claim is sent and answered **in seconds, while the patient is standing at the counter**.
lines.say: A U S pharmacy claim is sent and answered in seconds, while the patient is standing at the counter.

lines.raw: This is called **real-time adjudication**.
lines.say: This is called real-time adjudication.

lines.raw: The pharmacist knows the exact price before handing over the medicine.
lines.say: The pharmacist knows the exact price before handing over the medicine.

lines.raw: The same roles in three situations.
lines.say: The same roles in three situations.

lines.raw: Who writes the prescription? Ram (Nepal, private insurance): The hospital doctor. Sita (Nepal, SSF): The SSF-listed hospital doctor. Emily (USA): Dr. Patel (the **prescriber**).
lines.say: Who writes the prescription? Ram (Nepal, private insurance): The hospital doctor. Sita (Nepal, S S F): The S S F listed hospital doctor. Emily (U S A): Doctor Patel (the prescriber).

lines.raw: Who gives the medicine? Ram (Nepal, private insurance): A medical shop. Sita (Nepal, SSF): The hospital pharmacy. Emily (USA): A retail pharmacy.
lines.say: Who gives the medicine? Ram (Nepal, private insurance): A medical shop. Sita (Nepal, S S F): The hospital pharmacy. Emily (U S A): A retail pharmacy.

lines.raw: Who sends the claim? Ram (Nepal, private insurance): **Ram**, with the bill and prescription. Sita (Nepal, SSF): The **hospital**, inside its bill to SSF. Emily (USA): The **pharmacy**, electronically.
lines.say: Who sends the claim? Ram (Nepal, private insurance): Ram, with the bill and prescription. Sita (Nepal, S S F): The hospital, inside its bill to S S F. Emily (U S A): The pharmacy, electronically.

lines.raw: When is the price known? Ram (Nepal, private insurance): Weeks later, when the insurer reimburses. Sita (Nepal, SSF): At the counter (Sita pays 20%). Emily (USA): At the counter, in seconds.
lines.say: When is the price known? Ram (Nepal, private insurance): Weeks later, when the insurer reimburses. Sita (Nepal, S S F): At the counter (Sita pays 20 percent). Emily (U S A): At the counter, in seconds.

lines.raw: Ram's way exists in the US too.
lines.say: Ram's way exists in the U S too.

lines.raw: If a US patient uses a pharmacy outside their plan's network, or forgets their card, they may pay the full price and later mail a **paper claim form** with the receipt to get money back.
lines.say: If a U S patient uses a pharmacy outside their plan's network, or forgets their card, they may pay the full price and later mail a paper claim form with the receipt to get money back.

lines.raw: That is exactly what Ram does.
lines.say: That is exactly what Ram does.

lines.raw: It is the exception, though: almost all US pharmacy claims are electronic.
lines.say: It is the exception, though: almost all U S pharmacy claims are electronic.

lines.raw: Pharmacy benefit vs medical benefit.
lines.say: Pharmacy benefit versus medical benefit.

lines.raw: Here is a surprise for beginners: **not every drug ends up in pharmacy data**.
lines.say: Here is a surprise for beginners: not every drug ends up in pharmacy data.

lines.raw: It depends on **who gives the drug** and **where**.
lines.say: It depends on who gives the drug and where.

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: Where the drug is given. Pharmacy benefit: Picked up at a pharmacy and taken at home. Medical benefit: Given by a nurse or doctor in a clinic, hospital or infusion centre.
lines.say: Where the drug is given. Pharmacy benefit: Picked up at a pharmacy and taken at home. Medical benefit: Given by a nurse or doctor in a clinic, hospital or infusion centre.

lines.raw: Example. Pharmacy benefit: Amoxicillin capsules, cholesterol tablets. Medical benefit: An injection in the doctor's office, chemotherapy through a drip.
lines.say: Example. Pharmacy benefit: Amoxicillin capsules, cholesterol tablets. Medical benefit: An injection in the doctor's office, chemotherapy through a drip.

lines.raw: Which claim? Pharmacy benefit: **Pharmacy claim** (NCPDP format). Medical benefit: **Medical claim** (837P or 837I, see the Medical course).
lines.say: Which claim? Pharmacy benefit: Pharmacy claim (N C P D P format). Medical benefit: Medical claim (8 3 7 P or 8 3 7 I, see the Medical course).

lines.raw: Drug code. Pharmacy benefit: **NDC** (National Drug Code, lesson 4). Medical benefit: Usually a **HCPCS J-code**, like `J1100` (dexamethasone injection).
lines.say: Drug code. Pharmacy benefit: N D C (National Drug Code, lesson 4). Medical benefit: Usually a H C P C S J-code, like J 1 1 0 0 (dexamethasone injection).

lines.raw: Drugs hide in medical claims.
lines.say: Drugs hide in medical claims.

lines.raw: In June 2025, Emily had her appendix removed and stayed two nights in hospital.
lines.say: In June 2025, Emily had her appendix removed and stayed two nights in hospital.

lines.raw: The hospital billed **$800 of medicines** under revenue code `0250` (pharmacy).
lines.say: The hospital billed 800 dollars of medicines under revenue code 0 2 5 0 (pharmacy).

lines.raw: Those medicines are on the **medical** claim, not in pharmacy data.
lines.say: Those medicines are on the medical claim, not in pharmacy data.

lines.raw: If you want to know **all** the money spent on drugs, you must look in **both** places.
lines.say: If you want to know all the money spent on drugs, you must look in both places.

lines.raw: What does a pharmacy claim contain?
lines.say: What does a pharmacy claim contain?

scenes.section: What does a pharmacy claim contain?

lines.raw: Here is a quick table.
lines.say: Here is a quick table.

lines.raw: **Member details**. What it includes: Member ID, name, date of birth, plan details from the card. Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Emily Carter, member ID M1001.
lines.say: Member details. What it includes: Member I D, name, date of birth, plan details from the card. Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Emily Carter, member I D M 1 0 0 1.

lines.raw: **Prescriber details**. What it includes: Who wrote the prescription (NPI). Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Dr. Patel.
lines.say: Prescriber details. What it includes: Who wrote the prescription (N P I). Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Doctor Patel.

lines.raw: **Pharmacy details**. What it includes: Which pharmacy filled it (NPI and NCPDP ID). Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Main Street Pharmacy.
lines.say: Pharmacy details. What it includes: Which pharmacy filled it (N P I and N C P D P I D). Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Main Street Pharmacy.

lines.raw: **Drug details**. What it includes: Which drug (NDC code), how much, how many days it lasts. Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Amoxicillin 500 mg, 30 capsules, 10 days.
lines.say: Drug details. What it includes: Which drug (N D C code), how much, how many days it lasts. Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Amoxicillin 500 mg, 30 capsules, 10 days.

lines.raw: **Money details**. What it includes: Drug cost, pharmacy fee, what the patient and plan paid. Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Total $11.30: Emily $5.00, plan $6.30.
lines.say: Money details. What it includes: Drug cost, pharmacy fee, what the patient and plan paid. Example from Emily's amoxicillin: Total 11 dollars 30 cents: Emily 5 dollars, plan 6 dollars 30 cents.

scenes.section: What does a pharmacy claim contain?

lines.raw: What is missing?
lines.say: What is missing?

lines.raw: The diagnosis.
lines.say: The diagnosis.

lines.raw: A medical claim always says **why** (the ICD-10 diagnosis).
lines.say: A medical claim always says why (the I C D 10 diagnosis).

lines.raw: A pharmacy claim usually **does not**.
lines.say: A pharmacy claim usually does not.

lines.raw: Emily's amoxicillin claim does not say "strep throat".
lines.say: Emily's amoxicillin claim does not say "strep throat".

lines.raw: Analysts often link pharmacy claims to medical claims by **member and date** to guess the reason.
lines.say: Analysts often link pharmacy claims to medical claims by member and date to guess the reason.

lines.raw: How big is it?
lines.say: How big is it?

lines.raw: According to CMS, the US spent about **$450 billion** on **retail prescription drugs** in 2023, roughly **9%** of all US health spending.
lines.say: According to C M S, the U S spent about 450 billion dollars on retail prescription drugs in 2023, roughly 9 percent of all U S health spending.

lines.raw: That is more than **10 times** Nepal's entire economy.
lines.say: That is more than 10 times Nepal's entire economy.

lines.raw: Pharmacy claims are also the **most frequent** claims: many people never go to hospital in a year, but lots of people pick up a prescription every month.
lines.say: Pharmacy claims are also the most frequent claims: many people never go to hospital in a year, but lots of people pick up a prescription every month.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Pharmacy data = the record of prescription medicines picked up from a pharmacy.
lines.say: Pharmacy data = the record of prescription medicines picked up from a pharmacy.

lines.raw: In the US, the pharmacy sends the claim electronically and gets an answer in seconds: **real-time adjudication**.
lines.say: In the U S, the pharmacy sends the claim electronically and gets an answer in seconds: real-time adjudication.

lines.raw: Drugs taken at home are usually on the **pharmacy benefit**; drugs given in a clinic are usually billed on the **medical** claim with HCPCS J-codes.
lines.say: Drugs taken at home are usually on the pharmacy benefit; drugs given in a clinic are usually billed on the medical claim with H C P C S J-codes.

lines.raw: A pharmacy claim usually has **no diagnosis code**.
lines.say: A pharmacy claim usually has no diagnosis code.
